coverage.focus: World War I cause map: prewar tensions, the outbreak sequence, and a basic 1914 to 1918 chronology.
essentialIdeas: Prewar European alliances and tensions divided Europe into rival blocs and made local crises more dangerous.
The Sarajevo assassination triggered the July Crisis, which moved through ultimata and mobilization to declarations of war.
World War I began in 1914, the United States entered in 1917, and the armistice ended the fighting in 1918.

methodBriefing.what: Study a short model, explain it in your own words, repair any gap, then explain it again.
methodBriefing.why: It helps you build a connected story instead of memorizing disconnected facts.

activities.label: Big picture model
activities.title: Why Europe Pulled Toward War
activities.body: Read the model and note the main causes. Then move on to your own explanation.

essentialIdeas: Prewar European alliances and tensions divided Europe into rival blocs and made local crises more dangerous.

activities.label: Explain the cause map
activities.title: Explain the Alliance Map
activities.body: In your own words, explain how alliances and tensions made Europe more fragile. Keep it short and specific.
activities.correctAnswer: Europe was split into rival alliance blocs, and tensions made a local crisis more likely to spread into a larger war.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names rival blocs and explains why tensions made escalation easier. If needed, add one concrete tension such as arms buildup or rivalries.

activities.label: Fix the outbreak sequence
activities.title: From Sarajevo to War
activities.body: Use the cue to correct the sequence. State the outbreak chain in order.
activities.misconceptionSummary: The assassination itself was the war, so the rest of the July Crisis is not part of the outbreak sequence.
activities.concept: From Sarajevo to declarations of war
activities.correctAnswer: The Sarajevo assassination led to the July Crisis, which moved through ultimata and mobilization to declarations of war.
activities.feedback: The key correction is that the assassination started the crisis, not the whole war. A complete answer includes the July Crisis, mobilization, and declarations of war in order.

activities.label: Timeline in your words
activities.title: Explain the WWI Timeline
activities.body: Explain the start-to-finish timeline in plain language. Include the key dates and one simple cause-to-event link.
activities.correctAnswer: World War I began in 1914, the United States entered in 1917, and the armistice ended the fighting in 1918.
activities.feedback: A complete answer gives the three anchor dates in order and shows that they are events in the war's timeline, not causes.

activities.label: Quick recognition check
activities.title: Pick the Correct Timeline
activities.body: Choose the best timeline order. One option is correct.
choices: 1914 war begins, 1917 United States enters, 1918 armistice ends the fighting
1917 war begins, 1914 United States enters, 1918 armistice ends the fighting
1918 war begins, 1914 United States enters, 1917 armistice ends the fighting
1914 armistice ends the fighting, 1917 war begins, 1918 United States enters
activities.correctAnswer: 1914 war begins, 1917 United States enters, 1918 armistice ends the fighting
activities.feedback: The correct sequence is 1914, then 1917, then 1918. This checks the basic chronology of the war, not a deeper cause chain.

activities.label: Plan your return
activities.title: Return to the Timeline Later
activities.body: Write one sentence about what you want to review again after a delay. Keep it specific.

activities.label: Fix the outbreak sequence
activities.title: From Sarajevo to War
activities.body: Use the cue to correct the sequence. State the outbreak chain in order.
activities.concept: From Sarajevo to declarations of war
activities.correctAnswer: The Sarajevo assassination led to the July Crisis, which moved through ultimata and mobilization to declarations of war.
activities.feedback: The key correction is that the assassination started the crisis, not the whole war. A complete answer includes the July Crisis, mobilization, and declarations of war in order.

activities.label: Timeline in your words
activities.title: Explain the WWI Timeline
activities.body: Explain the start-to-finish timeline in plain language. Include the key dates and one simple cause-to-event link.
activities.correctAnswer: World War I began in 1914, the United States entered in 1917, and the armistice ended the fighting in 1918.
activities.feedback: A complete answer gives the three anchor dates in order and shows that they are events in the war's timeline, not causes.

activities.label: Quick recognition check
activities.title: Pick the Correct Timeline
activities.body: Choose the best timeline order. One option is correct.
choices: 1914 war begins, 1917 United States enters, 1918 armistice ends the fighting
1917 war begins, 1914 United States enters, 1918 armistice ends the fighting
1918 war begins, 1914 United States enters, 1917 armistice ends the fighting
1914 armistice ends the fighting, 1917 war begins, 1918 United States enters
activities.correctAnswer: 1914 war begins, 1917 United States enters, 1918 armistice ends the fighting
activities.feedback: The correct sequence is 1914, then 1917, then 1918. This checks the basic chronology of the war, not a deeper cause chain.

activities.label: Plan your return
activities.title: Return to the Timeline Later
activities.body: Write one sentence about what you want to review again after a delay. Keep it specific.

activities.title: Check today's ideas again later
